Black Beach Update

By: Annalise Lubbe | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
... How did two South African engineers working in Equatorial Guinea end up getting a twelve year prison sentence for a crime they say they have not committed?

Unique Selling Point:
When Frederik Potgieter and Peter Huxam, two South African engineers working for an offshore oil and gas company in Equatorial Guinea were thrown in jail in the middle of the night on trumped up drug charges little did they know how it would turn out. After having spent four months in prison without any concrete proof as evidence they were found guilty of drug smuggling and were ordered to pay a fine of five million US dollars each and a 2.5 million dollar fine combined for court charges. Their families were inconsolable as they believed in their innocence.

Summary:
In March, we covered the story of the two South African engineers who were thrown in jail on trumped up drug charges after Teodorin Obiang, the Vice President of Equatorial Guinea’s superyacht was seized in Cape Town harbor. It was a matter of tit for tat as no evidence was found that linked Frederick Potgieter and Peter Huxum to drug smuggling. At the time they were employees of a Dutch oil and gas company in Equatorial Guinea, but had never met yet were arrested at the same hotel and sent to Black Beach prison. Their employees appointed a legal team to assist in the investigation of the charges they faced. They have been in prison since February this year.

Further information:
The superyacht was released and sent back to Equatorial Guinea but there are still two properties in Cape Town owned by Obiang who is embroiled in a legal suit against another South African. Daniel Janse van Rensburg sued Obian for R30 million for wrongful imprisonment and abuse in Black Beach prison in 2015 after he was wrongfully accused and spent two years in that hell without any formal charges.

Frederick and Peter were moved from Black Beach prison to a high security prison on the mainland meant for hard core political prisoners. It is no secret that the vice president, Obiang, uses his political power to influence the judges. It therefore came as no surprise that on Friday last week, during a state television announcement in Equatorial Guinea, the two men, now visibly thinner and clean shaven head, had to face their sentence: 12 years in prison and a hefty fine. They are to pay 5 million Us dollars each plus the court fee of 2.5 million us dollars. The sentence is three times longer than the usual for a crime of this nature. Plus they have to pay a fine.

The South African embassy in Equatorial Guinea have made no effort to attend the hearing or speak on their behalf, nor have they visited the men at all in prison.

The families are shocked beyond belief. They were hoping that the release of the yacht would set the men free as Obiang now had his way. But it seems that the two properties which are part of the R30 millionaire lawsuit brought against Obiang by van Vuuren, are still being used as pawns.

There is no independent judicial system in Equatorial Guinea. If you go against the president and his family you will pay the consequences, said a former judge who fled for his life. Political pressure will be used to keep people locked up without evidence.

The story: We will recap on the previous events which lead to the arrest and imprisonment of Peter and Frederik, the two engineers who were charged for alleged drug smuggling in Equatorial Guinea. Additional material to ad to the story in the update: the Court sentencing document; the TikTok video clip of the two men being sentenced in a court in Equatorial Guinea; the official statement of the employees of the two engineers and a short interview with Francois Nigrini, the family spokesperson who will speak on behalf of Peter and Frederiks’ family. We will use up sounds from the loved ones: Frederik’s daughter, Joelene whom we interviewed on how she feels about the terrible fate of her father in prison which they clearly believe he is not guilty of. We also have up-sounds of Kathy, Peter’s wife who was in total disbelief about the drug charges and called Peter a ‘family man’ who loved his granddaughter and was looking forward to coming home when they arrested him. The interview with the family spokesperson will be on Teams as he is based in Pretoria and we do not have time to arrange for a sitdown interview with a cameraman. The employers of Peter and Frederik. SBM Offshore, an Offshore OIl and Gas company in Equatorial Guinea have been providing legal services for the two men and will be appealing their court verdict. We have also sent a request to DIRCO to give us their response on the outcome of the sentence of the two South African citizens.

FINAL SCRIPT: Script: Black Beach - follow up
Date 15 July 2023
Duration: 4.23 minutes

V/O On the 9th of February two South African engineers were arrested in their hotel room in Malabo, the capital of Equatorial Guinea, and detained on drug charges. The two men were working for a Dutch oil and gas company, SBM Offshore, and were preparing to return home when they were sent to the notorious Black Beach prison.

A local news channel said they were in possession of cocaine.

Up sound:
Frederik Potgieter; “Never in my life”
Peter Huxham: “It’s not mine”

V/O Equatorial Guinea is ruled by a dictatorship. There is no independent judiciary and power rests with the president and his son, Vice President Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue, who is in charge of the country’s security and prisons. A decade ago a South African businessman, Daniel Janse van Rensburg, spent two years in Black Beach prison after a business deal with one of the president's family members went sour. On Daniel’s release, he sued Obiang for illegal incarceration and suffering. Two properties in Cape Town and a superyacht called Blue Shadow were attached

LINK: Forty Eight hours after Obiang’s superyacht was attached at Cape town harbour Peter and Frederik were arrested on the other side of the continent. Was this a cruel game of tit-for-tat?

VO Within days, the men were moved from Black Beach to Ovang Asem in Mongomo on the mainland: a maximum security prison known to house political prisoners….
Since the 9th of February, Peter and Frederik have had no contact with their famillies. No phone calls, no messages. Jolene, Frederik’s daughter, misses her dad terribly.

Jolene Potgieter: Elke dag, as ek iets gedoen het stuur ek vir hom a WhatsApp al kry hy dit nie. (Every day if I do something, I send him a WhatsApp - even if he won’t get it.)

LINK: In March, much like the families, we were hopeful that they would be reunited soon. But recent sinister developments may have sealed their fate.

V/O On the 30th of June, a gaunt Peter and Frederik were convicted. They were sentenced by the Mongomo court to 12 years in prison and $5M USD each in damages with an additional $2.5M USD fine to be shared. They were found guilty of “Trafficking and illicit possession of drugs (cocaine)”.

Jolene Potgieter: Frederik’s daughter - Toe ons die video sien van my pa wat by die hof was, (When we saw the video of my dad in court,) was dit regtig vir ons moeilik (it was really difficult for us.)….Toe ons sien hoeveel gewig hy verloor het (When we saw how much weight he’d lost,) en hoe hartseer hy lyk (and how sad he looked,) het dit ons harte gebreek.(it broke our hearts.)

V/O Peter’s wife Kathy, was grief stricken.

Vanessa Nigrini: Kathy’s sister: When she heard the sentence she was almost hospitalised with a nervous breakdown. She is devastated. She is really really heartbroken.

VO: Vanessa and her husband Francois have been appointed as spokespeople for Peter’s family. They’ve been desperately working with SBM to free the men.

Francois Nigrini: Peter’ stepbrother - Obviously the first plan is to, and it was executed already, is to appeal the sentence. 00;07;59;02 It’s unbelievable that a court can rule so harshly on two innocent people.

V/O SBM Offshore has appointed a legal team to represent Peter and Frederik and has been in daily contact with the two families. In a statement, the company said it will continue to provide legal support to the men.

SBM statement on screen

VO: But apart from their legal team and a doctor, no one has been to see them.
The Department of International Relations and Cooperation said that the South African Embassy has been illegally denied access to the prisoners, and that DIRCO is willing to engage constructively with the government of Equatorial Guinea.
The situation is taking its toll: Peter suffered an apparent heart attack some weeks ago, and was hospitalised.

Link: Dawn often symbolises hope and new beginnings, but for Peter and Frederik’s devastated families caught in the middle of a political game, there’s no knowing what the future holds.

__________________________________________________________________________

Promo one: 21 seconds

Vanessa Nigrini: We are shocked. We are devastated.

V/O Two South Africans, for the last five months imprisoned in Equatorial Guinea on what their families say are false charges. Now, they’ve received more devastating news.

Vanessa Nigrini: around 17.53 We just can’t believe that they got that sentence especially because they are innocent.

Promo two: 21 seconds
VO: An arrest on dubious drug charges. A stint in a notorious prison. And now a shattering verdict.

Jolene Potgieter: Ek het eintlik stomgeslaan. (I was dumbfounded.) Dit was asof daar n baksteen op jou rug gegooi word (It was like someone loaded bricks on your back.)


VO: Are these devastated families being used as pawns in a political game of tit for tat?

Francois Nigrini: We must get to the point where we can prove their innocence.
